newsitem.title: UK: Report said to cast doubt on UK Labour jobs scheme.
newsitem.headline: Report said to cast doubt on UK Labour jobs scheme.

text.p: An independent report this week will cast doubt on the ability of Britain's opposition Labour Party to fulfil its pledge to create 250,000 new jobs for young people through a windfall tax on the profits of privatised utilities, according to Sunday newspapers.

The report by the National Institute for Economic and Social Research, due to be published on Wednesday, will also warn that big tax rises will be needed to control public borrowing by the turn of the century even if public spending is kept on a tight rein.

The Mail on Sunday said the report suggests that only about 100,000 new jobs will be created by the proposed windfall tax scheme as some employers will lay off existing staff to take advantage of the new government subsidies.

The report acknowledges there would be some savings in tax and benefits from the scheme. But according to the Mail on Sunday, it adds "It is questionable whether it is, in fact, the cheapest way of reducing long-term unemployment."
The institute predicts that the first budget of a new Labour government would reduce advance corporation tax credits to 10 percent from 20 percent.
The Sunday Times said the Institute had calculated that Britain has an underlying or structural budget deficit of 2.5 percent of GDP.

It predicted that at the turn of the century a Labour government would be well above its "golden rule" PSBR (public sector borrowing requirement) target under which public borrowing should equal capital spending by government.
It said this implied a PSBR of six billion sterling and that, barring an even tougher public-spending regime, achieving either target would require tax increases.
The Institute's report is due to be released the day before Britain's general election on May 1.
